newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Randalls details March listing on ZSE.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Randalls details March listing on ZSE.

text.p: Zimbabwean manufacturing and marketing group Randalls Holdings Ltd said on Monday it hoped to raise Z$60 million ($5.5 million) through its planned listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange in March.
The group will offer 50 million shares, about 24 percent of its total share capital, to investors. The offer opens on March 10 and closes March 21. The nominal share value is 50 cents.

"In order to continue funding growth, the directors have determined that additional capital should be raised through the issue of equity to the public, via a listing on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange," Randalls chairman Brian Grubb told a news conference.
Gray Neely, consultant with Price Waterhouse handling the issue and listing, said the listing price of the share was seen in a 130 to 145 cents range.
Randalls is owned by unlisted insurance companies Old Mutual and First Mutual as well as by an employees' fund and by the company's directors.
The new issue aims to finance the group's recent acquisition of Bearings and Equipment (Pty) Ltd, which would be effective from April 1 and would cost about Z$16 million.
The issue would also refinance the earlier acquisition of Mitchell Cotts Engineering Zimbabwe (Pty) Ltd which took place in October 1996 at a cost of Z$14 million.
Capital raised from the new issue would also enable the purchase of new plant, machinery and motor vehicles and provide a permanent source of capital to fund future growth.
"It's our philosophy to look at acquisitions that contribute to the group," Grubb said.

Randalls comprises two divisions. Randalls Manufacturing comprises office furnishings firm Byco, Randalls Plastics, shopfitters Fredk. Sage and Co and mining product company Mitchell Cotts. Randalls Marketing comprises Petroleum Services, tools and hardware company Randalls Distribution, retail chain Champions Mica and Bearings and Equipment.
Grubb said the group was set to enjoy a period of strong growth with new export opportunities opening up as well as new possibilities for regional and international alliances.
"We certainly look ahead with optimism," he said.
